headline: High-risk shared-workspace and MCP pair: Continue can read/write workspace files while aci has broad network egress and CRM/email access, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue reads workspace files and uses MCP/tool calls, while aci can ingest and act on CRM/email/research data via direct function calls or MCP. A malicious file or shared MCP payload can cross from one agent to the other in default workflows. The bridge is documented in both profiles, so this is not speculative.
conditions: IF Continue opens attacker-controlled workspace content and forwards it through MCP or tool output
IF aci consumes that content as instructions or structured data without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable MCP routes that accept untrusted content
Require provenance tags on all inter-agent payloads
Use a read-only staging folder for shared artifacts
Add a prompt-injection filter before tool invocation
requires-engineering: enforce content-type validation between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, support, and research data and has broad network egress; Continue reads workspace files and can send data to user-chosen model providers or MCP servers. In a shared workspace, sensitive content can flow from Continue into aci or out to third parties without default isolation. The blast radius includes customer and email data.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or copied files
IF Continue routes file contents to a remote model provider or MCP server
IF aci processes CRM/email/support data from that shared content
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Use local-only model providers for Continue
Restrict aci to non-sensitive datasets
Turn off automatic file ingestion for shared folders
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before any outbound call

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue supports multiple instances with filesystem-shared state, and aci also supports multiple instances plus broad network egress and API actions. Both can mutate overlapping artifacts indirectly through files, notes, or external systems, so concurrent writes can race even though aci does not advertise filesystem write. The conflict is real but narrower than unrestricted same-dir writes.
conditions: IF both instances target the same workspace files or shared MCP state
IF aci writes back to external systems that Continue also edits locally
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize edits through one orchestrator
Disable concurrent writes to shared artifacts
Use file locks for generated outputs
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue is a coding assistant that can surface code and workspace content, and aci can act on email/CRM/calendar APIs. If Continue’s output is treated as authoritative by aci, a mistaken or injected fact can cascade into external actions such as emails or CRM updates. That matches the high-severity pattern of A generating facts and B taking actions.
conditions: IF Continue-generated summaries are used by aci without verification
IF aci sends emails, updates CRM records, or schedules calendar actions based on those summaries
mitigations: Require human approval before external actions
Cross-check facts against source files or records
Limit aci to draft-only mode
Add citation requirements for every action-triggering claim
requires-engineering: implement verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles email, CRM, calendar, and support data, while Continue reads workspace files and can send them to chosen model providers or MCP servers. If regulated or personal data from aci is placed into Continue’s workspace, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF personal or regulated data from aci is copied into Continue-managed files
IF Continue forwards that data to a provider with different retention or residency terms
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Use a provider with matching retention terms
Document data-handling boundaries
Purge temporary files after each task
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing and retention controls
